items.title: Why data center companies Equinix and Oracle are buying fuel cells
items.summary: The “speed to power” ambitions of big cloud computing service providers and data center companies are boosting installations of on-site fuel cells, particularly those made by Bloom Energy.

items.title: Heatwave and drought cost UK farmers £390m, research suggests
items.summary: This year's exceptionally hot and dry conditions may have cut UK harvests by almost £400m according to provisional estimates.

items.title: Defra: Plastic bag charge cut single-use sales by 98% at major retailers
items.summary: Since the bag charge was introduced in October 2015, sales of single-use plastic carrier bags have fallen 98% across leading retailers like Marks and Spencer and Tesco.

items.title: The new normal: How climate risk is reshaping property value
items.summary: Europe's worsening climate extremes are exposing a new financial risk.

items.title: CBAM costs for Indian steelmakers unlikely to be as high as first feared
items.summary: New research has found that fears among Indian policymakers and steel producers regarding cost compliance with the EU’s Carbon Border Adjustment Mechanism (CBAM) could be unfounded, with some producers able to benefit from low-carbon exports.

items.title: Factcheck: How nuclear, gas, wind and solar power are affected during heatwaves
items.summary: Heatwaves are becoming more likely and more intense due to climate change, impacting sources of power generation around the world as they work to meet increased demand.
